analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Warsh's silence could be counterproductive
key_insights: Chair Warsh wants the Fed to renounce forward guidance and is leading by example, but the rest of the FOMC is not following. BofA says Warsh's refusal to guide markets may be encouraging other FOMC members to speak more, not less.
There has been more Fedspeak in the last two weeks than in any two-week period since the start of 2025, measured by a two-week rolling sum of Fed speaker events (Bloomberg data).

With 19 FOMC participants holding a range of views, the Chair would normally signal whether hawks or doves are in ascendance. Without that signal, both sides may have an incentive to speak more often and more forcefully.
BofA argues that forceful remarks by hawks and doves, with no anchor from the Chair, could cause undue volatility in rates markets.
Williams and Jefferson's cautious tone led markets to price out an October hike before the September inflation data were released. BofA says the October pause increasingly looks like a mistake.

Hawks have been vocal since then. Waller opened the door to a 50bp hike in December, Goolsbee entertained the possibility that wage inflation could inflect upwards, and Musalem called for up to 100bp of additional hikes.
BofA's 4Q 2026 GDP tracking estimate is unchanged at 2.4% q/q saar after October housing starts. Its official 4Q forecast is 2.3%.
Today's calendar: initial jobless claims, Philadelphia Fed business outlook, leading indicators, and remarks from Hammack, Jefferson, Goolsbee, Barr, Barkin and Paulson.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh's approach of renouncing forward guidance leads by example and removes the Chair as a source of market signaling.
tension_points.bear_case: Without the Chair's anchor, hawks and doves both speak more and more forcefully, producing undue rates volatility. Fedspeak is at its highest two-week level since early 2025.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fedspeak volume falling back from its current two-week peak, or the Chair resuming signaling on whether hawks or doves are in ascendance.
